formal_record.question: A spiral of isosceles triangles is constructed counterclockwise, starting with the shaded triangle $B A C$, whose top angle is $\angle B A C=100^{\circ}$. Triangle $\triangle A B C$ is numbered 0. Each subsequent triangle (numbered 1, 2, $3, \ldots$ ) shares exactly one edge with the previous triangle, as shown. What is the number of the first triangle that precisely covers triangle $\mathrm{nr}$. 0?

The figure on the left consists of two rectangles. Two side lengths are marked: 11 and 13. The figure is cut into three parts along the two lines drawn inside. These can be put together to make the triangle shown on the right. How long is the side marked $\mathrm{x}$?

Five identical right-angled triangles can be arranged so that their larger acute angles touch to form the star shown in the diagram. It is also possible to form a different star by arranging more of these triangles so that their smaller acute angles touch. How many triangles are needed to form the second star?

A square with sides of length 10 is rolled without slipping along a line. The rolling stops when $P$ first returns to the line. What is the length of the curve that $P$ has travelled?
Choices:
A:$10 \pi$
B:$5 \pi+5 \pi \sqrt{2}$
C:$10 \pi+5 \pi \sqrt{2}$
D:$5 \pi+10 \pi \sqrt{2}$
E:$10 \pi+10 \pi \sqrt{2}$

The big rectangle shown is divided into 30 equally big squares. The perimeter of the area shaded in grey is $240 \mathrm{~cm}$. How big is the area of the big rectangle?
Choices:
A:$480 \mathrm{~cm}^{2}$
B:$750 \mathrm{~cm}^{2}$
C:$1080 \mathrm{~cm}^{2}$
D:$1920 \mathrm{~cm}^{2}$
E:$2430 \mathrm{~cm}^{2}$

The diagram shows a shaded quadrilateral $P Q R S$ drawn on a grid. Each cell of the grid has sides of length $2 \mathrm{~cm}$. What is the area of quadrilateral $P Q R S$?
Choices:
A:$96 \mathrm{~cm}^{2}$
B:$84 \mathrm{~cm}^{2}$
C:$76 \mathrm{~cm}^{2}$
D:$88 \mathrm{~cm}^{2}$
E:$104 \mathrm{~cm}^{2}$

A large square is divided into smaller squares, as shown. What fraction of the large square is shaded grey?
Choices:
A:$\frac{2}{3}$
B:$\frac{2}{5}$
C:$\frac{4}{7}$
D:$\frac{4}{9}$
E:$\frac{5}{12}$

A paper triangle with sides of lengths 3, 4, and 5 inches, as shown, is folded so that point $A$ falls on point $B$. What is the length in inches of the crease?
Choices:
A:$1+\frac{1}{2} \sqrt{2}$
B:$\sqrt{3}$
C:$\frac{7}{4}$
D:$\frac{15}{8}$
E:$2$
A construction of equal cubes is shown in the upper picture. After several cubes are removed, it has the form shown in the lower picture. How many cubes were removed?

The centers of the faces of the right rectangular prism shown below are joined to create an octahedron. What is the volume of the octahedron?

Choices:
A:$\frac{75}{12}$
B:$10$
C:$12$
D:$10\sqrt{2}$
E:$15$

In the adjoining figure of a rectangular solid, $\angle DHG=45^\circ$ and $\angle FHB=60^\circ$. Find the cosine of $\angle BHD$.

Choices:
A:$\frac{\sqrt{3}}{6}$
B:$\frac{\sqrt{2}}{6}$
C:$\frac{\sqrt{6}}{3}$
D:$\frac{\sqrt{6}}{4}$
E:$\frac{\sqrt{6}-\sqrt{2}}{4}$
The numbers on the faces of this cube are consecutive whole numbers. The sums of the two numbers on each of the three pairs of opposite faces are equal. The sum of the six numbers on this cube is

Fourteen white cubes are put together to form the figure on the right. The complete surface of the figure, including the bottom, is painted red. The figure is then separated into individual cubes. How many of the individual cubes have exactly four red faces?

A shape is created by joining seven unit cubes, as shown. What is the ratio of the volume in cubic units to the surface area in square units?

Choices:
A:1 : 6
B:7 : 36
C:1 : 5
D:7 : 30
E:6 : 25

A wedge is cut from a $6$-cm cylinder as shown by the dashed curve. Which answer choice is closest to the volume of the wedge in cubic centimeters?
Choices:
A:48
B:75
C:151
D:192
E:603

A solid right prism $ABCDEF$ has a height of $16$ and equilateral triangle bases with side length $12,$ as shown. $ABCDEF$ is sliced with a straight cut through points $M,$ $N,$ $P,$ and $Q$ on edges $DE,$ $DF,$ $CB,$ and $CA,$ respectively. If $DM=4,$ $DN=2,$ and $CQ=8,$ determine the volume of the solid $QPCDMN.$
